label: Melanoma_Invasive_Overview_NOS
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Invasive melanoma is a malignant tumor arising from melanocytes.
- Accounts for the majority of mortality due to skin cancer.
- Ultraviolet exposure is the primary etiological factor.
- Breslow depth is the most important prognostic factor.
- BRAF mutation testing is recommended for stage III-IV melanoma.

## Terminology
- Invasive melanoma refers to malignant melanocytic tumors penetrating the dermis.
- Historically termed melanose and fungoid disease (not recommended).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:** 
  - Malignant melanocytic neoplasm.
  - Presence of atypical melanocytes invading dermal tissue.
- **Desirable:** 
  - BRAF mutation.
  - Loss of CDKN2A.
  - Presence of TERT promoter mutation.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Ultraviolet exposure as a key factor.
- Multistep model involving genomic and environmental factors:
  - BRAF mutation.
  - CDKN2A loss leading to senescence escape.
  - TP53 mutation for apoptosis resistance.
  - TERTp mutation for immortalization [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Incidence has risen over the last 50 years.
  - Higher incidence in periequatorial regions [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- **Risk Factors:**
  - Family and personal history of melanoma.
  - Dysplastic nevus phenotype, including genetic predispositions [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Immunosuppression influences melanoma risk.
- **Sites:**
  - Occurs anywhere on the skin, including subungual locations.
  - Frequent in areas like the back in men and legs in women (Pathoutlines).
- **Prognosis:**
  - Breslow depth is crucial for prognosis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Microscopic
- Atypical melanocytes can be spindle-shaped or epithelioid.
- Features pagetoid spread and dermal invasion.
- Presence of mitoses and ulceration can be seen.

## Ancillary Tests
- **IHC Profile:**
  - Markers include Melan-A, SOX10, HMB45, and S100 [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
- **Genetic Alterations:**
  - Common mutations: BRAF, CDKN2A, TP53, and TERTp [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Halo Naevus:**
  - Distinguished by expansile pattern, cytological atypia, and mitoses [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Halo_Naevus.html).
- **Recurrent Naevus:**
  - Differentiated by history and clinical context [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html).
- **Nodular Melanoma:**
  - Unpigmented forms may mimic squamous cell carcinomas or sarcomas [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Nodular_Melanoma.html).
- **Mucosal Melanoma:**
  - Challenges in differentiation from primary tumors based on site and morphology [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Mucosal_Melanoma.html).
- **Melanoma Metastatic to the Skin:**
  - Differentiated by intradermal nodules and previous melanoma history [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).

cards.title: Conjunctival melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Conjunctival melanoma definition: Conjunctival melanoma is an invasive malignant melanocytic neoplasm arising in the conjunctiva. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: severe cytological and architectural atypia, exceeding that expected in a naevus. Desirable: mitoses, invasion of the cornea, extension into the skin, ulceration, tumour necrosis, pagetoid growth pattern; molecular features consistent with melanoma (PRAME positivity and loss of p16 on immunohistochemistry; chromosomal instability confirmed by FISH, TERT promoter mutations, etc.).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin definition: Metastatic melanoma in the skin is melanoma that has spread from a primary melanoma (cutaneous or extracutaneous) to the skin. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: an intradermal or subcutaneous nodule of malignant neoplastic melanocytes. Desirable: a history of melanoma; immunohistochemical and/or molecular confirmation in challenging cases; cytological, immunohistochemical, and genetic features similar to those of primary melanoma.

cards.title: Conjunctival melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Conjunctival melanoma Section: microscopic The histological features are similar to those of invasive melanoma in the skin or mucosa. The intraepithelial component can be nested, pagetoid, lentiginous, or (rarely) absent. It can extend well beyond the invasive component and can involve the skin and/or minor lacrimal glands and invade the cornea. The subepithelial component shows stromal invasion by nests or sheets of atypical melanocytes. Melanoma cells can show the entire spectrum of cytomorphology encountered in melanoma elsewhere, ranging from small naevoid cells to highly atypical pleomorphic melanocytes with spindle or epithelioid cytomorphology. Nuclei can be hyperchromatic with inconspicuous nucleoli or vesicular with prominent nucleoli. Ulceration, mitotic activity, angiotropism, satellite metastases, in-transit metastases, and neurotropism may be seen. A residual naevus may be present.

cards.title: Dermal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Dermal melanoma Section: ancillary_studies Neoplastic melanocytes express melanocytic markers, including melan-A, SOX10, HMB45, and S100.

cards.title: Naevoid melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Naevoid melanoma Section: ancillary_studies The immunohistochemistry is similar to that of low-CSD melanoma.

cards.title: Halo naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Halo naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis of involuting halo naevi includes other lichenoid interface reactions, such as those seen in lichenoid keratosis and melanoma with lichenoid inflammation. Findings suggestive of melanoma include the presence of a separate population of cells with an expansile pattern of growth; severe cytological atypia; and frequent mitoses, ulceration, or tumour necrosis. The halo phenomenon may occasionally involve other types of naevi, including dysplastic, Spitz, and congenital naevi, as well as melanomas. In most lesions, there is no intraepidermal melanocytic proliferation adjacent to the dermal component. If in situ or superficially invasive melanoma is present adjacent to a dermal lesion simulating halo naevus, the entire lesion is most likely melanoma.

cards.title: Recurrent naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Recurrent naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis includes melanoma, dysplastic naevus, sclerosing naevus, and dysplastic naevus with florid fibroplasia.

cards.title: Mucosal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucosal melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes dysplastic naevi and special-site naevi (see section Dysplastic naevus, and section Special-site naevi (of the breast, axilla, scalp, and ear)).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis of metastatic melanoma in the skin includes primary melanoma, primary dermal melanoma, and atypical naevus. Blue naevus–like metastases are difficult to distinguish from common or epithelioid blue naevus. The presence of cytologically atypical epithelioid melanocytes and mitotic figures can mimic blue naevus–like melanoma.

Mitogenic driver mutation (i.e., BRAF mutation)
Escaping primary senescence (i.e., CDKN2A loss)
Overcoming apoptosis (i.e., TP53 mutation)
Immortalization (i.e., TERTp mutation)

cards.title: High CSD melanoma — Essential features
cards.excerpt:
Presents as a flat, growing, irregularly pigmented lesion on chronically sun damaged skin, which may develop a raised, papular or nodular focus, indicating tumorigenic growth
Microscopically, a proliferation of intraepidermal melanocytes overlying solar elastosis and exhibiting crowded growth along the basal epidermis; irregular distribution of nests and effacement of epidermal rete with or without an underlying dermally invasive component
Immunohistochemistry for melanocytic markers (MelanA / MART1, SOX10, MITF, HMB45) may assist in identification of diagnostic architectural features and may distinguish the lesion from mimics
Prognosis is correlated with presence and depth of invasion, mitotic rate among invasive cells and presence / absence of ulceration

cards.title: High CSD melanoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Complete excision, accomplished via wide local excision, staged surgical excision or Mohs micrographic surgery (Dermatol Surg 2011;37:1210)
Excisions may utilize staged Mohs micrographic surgery (slow Mohs) with rush processing, examination of surgical margins and closure upon report of negative margins
Mohs surgeons may also utilize frozen sections with melanocytic immunohistochemistry for margin assessment (J Am Acad Dermatol 2021;84:196)
For in situ disease, topical therapies (including imiquimod) may be useful in the adjuvant setting or as primary treatment if unresectable (J Am Acad Dermatol 2015;72:1047)
Radiotherapy (Radiat Oncol 2020;15:174)
Consideration of sentinel lymph node biopsy (CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472)
